appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus curtly denies the duchesse de Guermantes any real insight ('Elle n'en a aucune, me répondit sèchement'), then demands as 'le premier sacrifice' that the narrator stay out of society, declares himself sole holder of the 'Sésame' to the Guermantes and to anyone worth knowing, and states 'Je serai juge et entends rester maître de l'heure'; flustered, the narrator's own question 'se posa sur mes lèvres autrement que je n'aurais voulu.'
appraisal_events.explanation: In one continuous, imperious speech, Charlus dismisses the duchesse's claimed judgment and asserts total control over the narrator's access to society, visibly unsettling the narrator, who cannot even phrase his question as intended.

appraisal_events.evidence: Charlus reveals his aunt was merely 'Mme Thirion' before assuming, without real right, the name 'marquise de Villeparisis' ('Du moment qu'on prend un nom auquel on n'a pas droit...'); the narrator states this 'acheva la chute qu'elle avait commencée dans mon esprit' and concludes she 'n'avait rien d'aristocratique' despite the grand connections around her.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's dismissive account of his aunt's bourgeois origin and self-assumed title, joined to the narrator's own explicit reflection, completes a clear, narrator-endorsed fall in how Mme de Villeparisis's rank is understood.

status_effects.explanation: He asserts full control over the narrator's future social access, positioning himself as sole judge and gatekeeper and extracting the narrator's compliance as a condition of his favor.
He is placed under Charlus's demands and control, visibly flustered to the point that his own question comes out differently than he intended.
Charlus flatly and dismissively denies the special insight the narrator had just attributed to her, reducing her to a woman who merely fancies herself influential.

Both Charlus's account of her unentitled, self-assumed title and the narrator's explicit conclusion that she had 'rien d'aristocratique' mark a clear fall in how her rank is understood, despite her grand surrounding connections.
